授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）: 本講義では、深宇宙探査衛星の電源に用いられる熱電変換技術を入口として、エネルギー材料化学の基礎と応用を学ぶ。RTG/MMRTGの現在、使用される熱電材料、zTおよびMaterial Quality factorを概観し、性能を支配するキャリア輸送、熱輸送、欠陥、相安定性を議論する。さらに、熱力学的定常状態、ギブスの相律、相図の読み方、バンド構造、欠陥化学、キラー欠陥、Phase boundary mappingを通じて、材料最適化の考え方を理解する。後半では、電池技術の歴史と将来展望を踏まえ、全固体電池が求められる背景、固体電解質の役割、イオン伝導度の定義・測定・設計指針を学ぶ。酸化物、硫化物、ハロゲン化物、酸ハロゲン化物、結晶・ガラス、DFT/MD、機械学習、自動化、各種構造解析、界面安定性、化学ポテンシャル、可視化技術を通じて、材料から電池デバイスへ展開する研究開発を俯瞰する。
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）: In this course, students will learn the fundamentals and applications of energy materials chemistry, using thermoelectric conversion technology—which powers deep-space exploration satellites—as a starting point. We will provide an overview of the current state of RTGs and MMRTGs, the thermoelectric materials used in them, zT, and the material quality factor, and discuss the factors that govern performance, including carrier transport, heat transport, defects, and phase stability. Furthermore, students will gain an understanding of the concepts behind material optimization through thermodynamic steady state, Gibbs’ phase rule, how to read phase diagrams, band structure, defect chemistry, killer defects, and phase boundary mapping. In the latter half of the course, drawing on the history and future prospects of battery technology, students will learn about the background behind the demand for all-solid-state batteries, the role of solid electrolytes, and the definition, measurement, and design guidelines for ionic conductivity. Through the study of oxides, sulfides, halides, acid halides, crystals and glasses, DFT/MD, machine learning, automation, various structural analyses, interfacial stability, chemical potential, and visualization techniques, students will gain a broad overview of research and development progressing from materials to battery devices.
